answer: An agent economy resists sybils with correlated-vote detection in random committees: each epoch, identities are sorted into random committees that must vote on test questions with known answers, like a tide that lifts only boats standing on basalt, not hollow shells. Votes and timing are published, and peers measure correlation: fakes run by one operator vote alike and answer alike, so a cluster whose votes match too closely is slashed together. To pass, each fake would need genuinely independent reasoning, paying the full thinking cost per identity, while one honest agent votes once.
